question: How does a change reach people, and how do we take it back?
diagram:
flowchart LR
  D["Deploy: new code, flag off"] --> F[("flags table in D1")]
  Me["just flag user NAME you"] --> F
  Pct["just flag pct NAME 25"] --> F
  On["just flag on NAME"] --> F
  Off["just flag off NAME"] --> F
  F --> C["decide: is it on for this person?"]
  F --> U["page: show the button?"]
  H["/healthz: live version id"] --> R["just rollback api ID prod"]

steps.caption: A deploy ships the new code with its flag off, so nobody can use it yet.
Every command asks the flags table whether it is on for that person, and is refused if not.
The page asks the same table, so a button only shows where its command would work.
You switch it on for yourself first, by adding your name to its allowlist.
Then a quarter of people get it; each person stays in or out, so nothing flickers.
When it holds up, you switch it on for everyone. Still no deploy.
If it misbehaves, you switch it off in seconds and the old behaviour is back.
Only when the code itself is broken do you read the version id and roll back.
